Hannah / Laura —

I reviewed the Aureon redline and flagged the primary areas of concern that will require either commercial concessions or engineering controls:

1) Controller/Processor recharacterization: Aureon is pushing language that shifts obligations toward Processor beyond instructions. We should push back and offer clarifying language that preserves processor status but commits to documented processing only per Order Form scopes.

2) 24-hour breach notification: operationally aggressive. We can accept 24-hour initial notification for confirmed incidents affecting PHI but need 72 hours for investigations and a remediation/impact summary. Suggest: 24-hour hold-notify for confirmed data exposures, 72-hour follow-up report.

3) EU residency / TIA: We can prepare a TIA addendum that maps our SCC implementation, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS design, and region pinning to Aureon’s controls. If they require hard EU-only hosting for certain workloads, we can offer a dedicated region binding as an Order Form option (pricing impact).

4) Subprocessors and audit rights: we cannot commit to prior approval for all downstream subprocessors. Propose a notification and short-list approval process for subprocessors that will process PHI (we’ll provide a temporary list and a 10-business-day review window).

Next steps / timeline: I will produce a redline of their document and a proposed TIA by EOD Tuesday (2026-11-17). If sales needs a faster timeline, we can escalate to exec legal for a prioritized review.
